title: Storage of Plasma Functionalized Surfaces on CryoEM Specimen Supports for Years
content: Sample preparation is the major bottleneck in electron microscopy, this is especially true when applied to biological problems, such as solving structures of protein specimens. Routinely in cryomicroscopy, surfaces such as gold, amorphous carbon, or silicon dioxide are used. To control the wetting such that a specimen can be frozen in a thin film of amorphous water, a plasma treatment is used to remove contamination from the surface or otherwise decrease the liquid contact angle of the surface. In other cases the problem of achieving a suitable orientation distribution of proteins can be solved by controlling the surface chemistry of a support film such as graphene, and this functionalization can also be a incorporated into the plasma treatment process [1-3].
